checks.classification: non-obvious footgun for facet 2b, documented behaviour for facet 2a

checks.note: In-scope code at c5ad56d. Reproduced by a passing PoC, work/test/audit23/BonfireCapFrontRun.t.sol.

findings.reasoning: This is not a reckless admin mistake. Facet 2b is the core of the finding: an owner who wants to shrink a large pot will naturally call setMaxPayout(cap) on the live contract, and a holder can front-run it with burn() and collect the uncapped pot (PoC pays 250e18 instead of 10e18). A competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised that a protective setter can be defeated this way. Nothing in the setter or the story warns about it. So it is a Law-3 footgun and stays in scope. Facet 2a (unpause, or wiring complete, while uncapped hands the whole pause-period pot to the first burner) is weaker. Story-053 L99 says accrual continues through pause, L77 names maxPayout as the idle-period protection, and an owner who reads the story knows the default is uncapped. Taken alone, 2a is close to documented, obvious behaviour. It belongs in the finding as context and safe-config guidance, not as a second vector.
caveats: Safe owner sequences exist without the global Pauser. setRatePerDay(0), then setMaxPayout(cap), then restore the rate: one owner tx stops burns and preserves the pot (L98, L127-131). pause, then cap, then unpause works once a pauser is set. The finding's recommendation already says this. The QA write-up must not imply that the owner has no safe path; the hazard is only the reactive cap applied while burns are live.

Total emission is bounded by ratePerDay x elapsed time, which the owner budgeted; the invariant holds over about 1.09M calls. The loss is a missed forfeiture (phUSD dilution of rate x D - cap), not extraction beyond budget. This keeps it at Low and below Medium. The ECON-005 suppression guard against the 'opportunity cost' memory rule is correct, because AM is redeemable into unbacked phUSD.

maxPayout==0 by default is mandated by the spec (story L108/L114), so the 'optional hardening' recommendation (revert setRatePerDay(nonzero) while maxPayout==0) is a story change, not a code bug. Frame it as a recommendation for the phStaging2 deploy story, not as a deviation.

findings.reasoning: This is a scope question, and the answer is: in scope as a ycn ledger entry with the fix routed elsewhere. The code at c5ad56d is correct. NFTMinterV2.mintFor is authorized-only by design. The defect is that the deployed state retains an authorization (NFTMigrator 0x22c0fc1a) that the owner retired from the address book in phStaging2 story-059. Story-053's new burn-for-pot path turns that dormant authorization into a cheap route to a redeemable ticket. Dropping it as 'deployment-config only' would hide a live, unmonitored mint path into a value-bearing token, which Law 1 forbids. The owner would plausibly be surprised that a retired migrator now mints bonfire tickets, so it is a footgun rather than an obvious misconfiguration. The routing and fixLocus text (later ycn rescans are not an incomplete fix) is correct and mirrors L-27.
findings.valueClaimAssessment: Partly demonstrated. The fork simulation (V1.mint status 1, migrate status 1, V2 balanceOf(user,5)==1, V1 idx5 price 17,624 to 19,738 sats) is reported only in narrative form. ECON-003 says 'commands in the run transcript' and forkSimulation is null, so no persisted artifact or PoC exists. Under the 'subagent tool output is not evidence' rule, the migrate-route reproduction is unverified by artifact. The historical NFTMigrator logic (git show df4d590: migrate burns V1 and calls v2.mintFor) makes it highly plausible. Also, about $3.6 is the ticket COST, not value extracted. Realized value is the bonfire pot, which is zero until NFTBonfire is wired, and which about 772 idle V2 NFTs already undercut as a burn source.
caveats: Persist the fork reproduction as a work/ script or test, or downgrade 'fork-verified' to 'on-chain reads plus a historical-source trace', before promoting status from draft.
Impact is conditional on phStaging2 wiring NFTBonfire with a pot above about $3.6. State this conditionality in the QA text. The 'value-bearing' wording in the title is forward-looking.
The primary harm is revenue diversion to V1 dispatchers plus bypassed V2 price growth, not loss. That supports Low/QA.

checks.note: The minPayout=0 loss facet only. This facet is invalid as an impact.
Story-053 L100 and L136 accept that the pot is trivially front-runnable.

findings.reasoning: Two claims need to be kept apart. (1) 'A user who passes minPayout=0 and is front-run loses the NFT' is a user-input choice against a documented opt-out (NatSpec L95, story L136), so it is INVALID as a loss vector under C4. The record already labels it that way and does not count it as impact. (2) The finding's actual content is that the pot is winner-takes-all per block on a value-blind gate. The story explicitly accepts this, and the code matches (minPayout reverts at L101 before the burn at L106, so an honest front-run burner loses gas only). Accepted design with no asset loss is informational at best. It survives as valid QA only because it carries a concrete, actionable obligation for the unwritten phlimbo-ui burn-button story: default minPayout to pendingPayout() minus tolerance, never 0. If the UI passes 0, that is a UI defect, not a user mistake, which is why the note is worth keeping.
caveats: The QA text must not present the minPayout=0 loss as an impact.

NFTBonfire is unpausable until setPauser, and pausing NFTMinterV2 does not stop NFTMinterV2.burn, which is the bonfire's path. An owner who 'pauses the NFT system' through the global Pauser would be surprised that bonfire burns and AM mints continue, so it is a valid footgun note. NFTBonfire is not yet deployed or wired on mainnet, so there is no present exposure. The remaining issue is a documented operational gap with safe-config guidance. That is QA, which is how it is classed.
